text: Univ. of California, Riverside Data Management Plan
label: document_title

text: 1. Policy and Practice
label: section

text: The Bourns College of Engineering (BCOE) at the University of California, Riverside, in partnership with the UCR
label: content

text: Libraries and the California Digital Library, has established a new, custom data management system designed to
label: content

text: make results of our research readily and reliably accessible. This system combines two services of the California
label: content

text: Digital Library for the first time: an eScholarship series, a curated site where all BCOE investigators can store and
label: content

text: disseminate their data, and EZID permanent identifiers for long-term identification and management of data
label: content

text: resources.
label: content

text: All principal investigators in BCOE are responsible for complying with sponsor policies regarding data
label: content

text: management and accessibility. All have sufficient computing resources to store and process the data generated in
label: content

text: their research. Every principal investigator has the ability to create his or her personal web site, and to make data sets
label: content

text: available through that web site. Additionally, the eScholarship series (http://escholarship.org/uc/bcoe) provides a
label: content

text: ready-made resource for dissemination. Researchers can submit materials to the eScholarship series site, where it is
label: content

text: automatically given an EZID persistent identifier. All material on the site is indexed on Google, Google Scholar, and
label: content

text: Melvyl/WorldCat. The California Digital Library also provides data backup services to avoid accidental loss of data.
label: content

text: This partnership, which has resulted in the development of a new service that CDL can provide to other research
label: content

text: organizations, makes our data widely available and searchable under the taxonomies, identifiers, and standards of
label: content

text: universal data sharing systems envisioned for the near future (see Changing the Conduct of Science in the
label: content

text: Information Age, NSF, June 2011).
label: content

text: 2. Scope
label: section

text: This Data Management Plan addresses the NSF policy that primary data “commonly accepted in the scientific
label: content

text: community as necessary to validate research findings” be made available at little or no cost to the PI or project. In
label: content

text: accordance with this policy and guidance from the Office of Management and Budget, this plan does not include
label: content

text: preliminary analyses (including raw data), drafts of scientific papers, plans for future research, peer reviews, or
label: content

text: communications with colleagues. Data that must be withheld long enough to enable peer review and
label: content

text: publication/dissemination or protection of intellectual property is subject to this plan only after those steps have taken
label: content

text: place. Data will be available for access and sharing as soon as is reasonably possible, and no later than two years after
label: content

text: its acquisition. The data will be preserved for at least three years beyond the award period, as required by NSF
label: content

text: guidelines.
label: content

text: The release of data about students or any other human subjects is subject to policies and restrictions in protocols
label: content

text: adopted by the relevant Institutional Research Board (IRB) and the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act
label: content

text: (FERPA) regulations.
label: content

text: The proposed project will develop programming, compiler, and runtime support for applications, as described in
label: content

text: this proposal. The implementations will be made available to other researchers. All code will be preserved and
label: content

text: maintained for a minimum of three years beyond the award period as required by NSF guidelines. In addition,
label: content

text: sample adaptive versions of applications that will be developed in this work will also be made available.
label: content

text: 3. Data and Metadata Format and Content
label: section

text: The software will be made available in source code form and so will the applications developed. This will allow other
label: content

text: researchers to so not only use it but also modify it for their use. All materials uploaded to the eScholarship site from
label: content

text: UCR will be tagged uniformly with metadata about the source and nature of the data. Any electronic file format (e.g.,
label: content

text: text, spreadsheets, images) can be accepted. As a service to assure that materials are formatted correctly, a curator
label: content

text: from the College reviews all submissions before they are accepted.
label: content

text: 4. Accessibility and Data Protection
label: section

text: Materials will be searchable through a number of databases and search engines, including Google and Google
label: content

text: Scholar. As noted in Section 2 (Scope), data will be made available only after appropriate steps have been taken to
label: content

text: protect intellectual property. Confidential material will be handled according to policies and protocols for human
label: content

text: subjects, FERPA, and any other applicable regulations and restrictions.
label: content

text: Stored materials are downloadable but not editable, and they are backed up to assure no loss of data. All uploads are
label: content

text: approved by a curator before they are published.
label: content

text: 5. Derivative Products
label: section

text: All materials will contain acknowledgement of NSF support as per NSF policy: “This material is based upon work
label: content

text: supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant No. (NSF grant number).” Additionally, materials will
label: content

text: contain a disclaimer that “any opinions, findings, and conclusions or recommendations expressed in this material are
label: content

text: those of the author(s) and do not necessarily reflect the views of the National Science Foundation.”
label: content

text: In keeping with standard ethical practices, it is expected that subsequent users of the data will acknowledge the
label: content

text: source.
label: content

text: 6. Archiving and Access
label: section

text: If the PI leaves UCR, the products in the eScholarship series will remain stored there. PI is free to reproduce and
label: content

text: repost these materials at his/her new institution.
